title: files:dependencies lists every library and executable path, built or not
claim: Verdict: kept. The task prints the static libraries, dynamic libraries and executables of every spec. In the experiment it listed `dependencies/Vend/libvend.a` although nothing built it.

title: Mixin names resolve through user load paths, the project file's directory, then Unity's targets
claim: Verdict: kept. `Composinator#loadinate` appends `File.dirname(project_filepath)` and the built-in Unity targets directory to the user load paths and deduplicates by expanded path. `BUILTIN_MIXIN_LOAD_PATHS` holds the Unity `test/targets` directory.

title: Mixin and mixin-variable file paths are relative to the working directory
claim: Verdict: kept. Filepaths go to `File.exist?` as written, so they resolve against the working directory. The mixin directory fallback uses the project file's own directory.

title: A mixin simple name is told from a filepath by extension or the forward slash only
claim: Verdict: untestable here (Windows). `PathValidator#filepath?` returns true for a value with an extension or one containing `File::SEPARATOR`, which is `/` on every platform. The docs say "no path separator" and the project docs accept `\`. Whether a Windows `--mixin bar\base` (no extension) reaches this test unstandardized was not traced.

title: A mixin's list entries land before the base list, except tool arguments
claim: Verdict: kept. `RecursiveMerger` builds `mixin_val + config_val` for lists and `config_val + mixin_val` for `:tools` ↳ `<tool>` ↳ `:arguments`. A higher-priority mixin's `:paths` entries therefore come first. Search order inside the merged list is not changed afterwards.

title: Mixin load paths are searched top-down and each path tries every YAML extension
claim: Verdict: kept. `load_paths.product(yaml_extensions)` yields every extension of the first path before the next path.

title: A test suite needs :paths :include and/or TEST_INCLUDE_PATH, and no :include entry is required
claim: Verdict: kept. A project with no `:paths` ↳ `:include` passes validation. A test using `TEST_INCLUDE_PATH(include)` built and passed. The same project without the macro stopped with `Found no file `foo.h` in search paths`.

title: A release build needs :paths :test although the project file docs list only :build_root and :paths :source
claim: Verdict: broken. A project with `:release_build: TRUE`, `:project` ↳ `:build_root` and `:paths` ↳ `:source`, and no `:paths` ↳ `:test`, stops with `Required config file entry :paths ↳ :test does not exist.` The check lists `:paths` ↳ `:test` for every build.

title: Second-tier keys ending in _path or _paths get Ruby expansion and standard separators
claim: Verdict: kept. `eval_paths` expands every second-tier key that matches `/_path(s)?$/` under each top-level section, and `standardize_convention_paths` standardizes the same set. `:project` ↳ `:build_root`, :release_build ↳ :artifacts` and `:paths`/`:files` are handled by their own lines.

title: Which Ceedling picks WHICH_CEEDLING, then :which_ceedling, then vendor/ceedling, then the gem, with ~ expanded
claim: Verdict: kept. `InstallationSelector#select` takes the first of the environment variable, the config value and `vendor/ceedling` and falls back to the launcher's own root. `validate` standardizes the value, which expands `~`. Every experiment log here shows `Launching Ceedling from /home/user/Ceedling/` from `:which_ceedling`.
